# Affine centroid graphs: an exact face criterion for equality
not the general OC proof. The affine-centroid hypothesis is essential
for the exact two-sided criterion; general actual fibers do not satisfy
it. Sections1--5 independently PASS in
`unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`. The later extension
below is separately flagged for audit.

Let P be a finite nonempty subset of a Euclidean base space E. At each
p in P put a full-dimensional compact convex body K_p in R^d, d>=1,
with volume w_p>0. Let M=sum w_p. Suppose its centroid g_p is the
restriction of an affine function G:E->R^d. Set Gamma=(d/(d+1))^d.
No compatibility of these fibers is needed for the following statements.

For 0<alpha<=M call p in P an alpha-center of the weighted base if every closed
base halfspace containing p has weight at least alpha. Let F_p be the
minimal face of B=conv(P) containing p, including B itself. Write
w(F)=sum_{z in P intersect F} w_z. A polytope point is in the relative
interior of its minimal face.

## 1. Exact equality criterion at a specified weighted base center

If p is an alpha-center, then the raw mixed halfspace depth at
y=(p,g_p) is at least Gamma alpha. Moreover it equals Gamma alpha
if and only if both of the following hold:

1. w(F_p)=alpha;
2. there is one unit u in R^d such that, for EVERY z in P intersect F_p,

       |K_z intersect {x:u.(x-g_z)>=0}|=Gamma w_z.       (1)

In particular, if w(F_p)>alpha, the raw depth at this actual point is
STRICTLY greater than Gamma alpha. Strictness is about the infimum over
all halfspaces; it is not merely a separate strict inequality for each
fixed halfspace.

### Proof

The affine shear (z,x)->(z,x-G(z)) preserves all ambient halfspaces and
each fiber volume. Thus assume every g_z=0 and y=(p,0). A containing
halfspace may be moved parallel to its boundary until its boundary
contains y, decreasing its intersection with the measured set. A
nonvertical such halfspace has the form

       a.(z-p)+u.x>=0,   |u|=1.                        (2)

Let J={z:a.(z-p)>=0}. Its weight is at least alpha. At each z in J
the fiber halfspace contains its centroid, so ordinary Grunbaum gives
at least Gamma w_z. Summation proves the lower bound. A vertical
halfspace has mass at least alpha>Gamma alpha.

Suppose a sequence of containing halfspaces has masses tending to
Gamma alpha. Since alpha>Gamma alpha, all late members can be taken
nonvertical. Move them through y and normalize as in (2). Pass to a
subsequence for which u_j->u, the finite sign set
J={z:a_j.(z-p)>=0} is fixed, and each threshold
t_{j,z}=-a_j.(z-p) converges in the extended real line. The compactness
used here is only that of the unit sphere, the finite set of sign
patterns, and the finite product [-infinity,infinity]^P.

For a finite threshold limit t_z, fiber cap volumes converge by
dominated convergence: the limiting hyperplane has zero d-volume.
For limits plus/minus infinity they converge respectively to zero/full
fiber volume, by boundedness of K_z. Thus the limiting total mass is
the sum of these finitely many limiting cap volumes.

For z in J we have t_z<=0 and limiting mass at least Gamma w_z. For
t_z<0 this inequality is strict. Indeed 0 is in the interior of K_z,
so lowering a through-centroid cut by any positive distance adds
positive volume (or gives full volume, also strictly larger). Equality
of the total with Gamma alpha therefore implies

       w(J)=alpha, t_z=0 for z in J,
       limiting cap volume at z outside J is zero.     (3)

It also implies (1) for every z in J. At z outside J a zero limiting
cap volume requires t_z>=h_{K_z}(u)>0, or t_z=plus infinity. The strict
positivity follows from the interior centroid. In particular t_{j,z}
is bounded below by a positive constant for all late j.

There is a representation p=sum_{z in P intersect F_p} lambda_z z
with EVERY lambda_z>0 and sum lambda_z=1. To see this, for each z in
that finite set choose a small epsilon_z>0 with
(p-epsilon_z z)/(1-epsilon_z) in F_p, possible because p is in its
relative interior. Represent the latter point by vertices of F_p,
then average these representations of p. Every listed z receives a
positive coefficient. A singleton face is immediate.

For this representation sum lambda_z t_{j,z}=0 for every j. Terms
in J tend to zero; any term outside J is eventually bounded below by
a positive constant; all other terms outside J are nonnegative.
Consequently (3) forces P intersect F_p subset J.

Every face of a polytope is exposed by a linear functional. A closed
supporting halfspace meeting B exactly in F_p contains p, so the
alpha-center property gives w(F_p)>=alpha. This is immediate with
w(F_p)=M>=alpha when F_p=B. Together with (3) and the preceding
containment, this gives w(F_p)=w(J)=alpha and J=P intersect F_p,
because all weights are positive. This proves necessity, including
the claimed strictness of the infimum when w(F_p)>alpha.

Conversely suppose conditions 1 and 2. If F_p=B, the cap u.x>=0
already has mass Gamma alpha. Otherwise choose a base affine
functional l with l=0 on F_p and l<0 at all other points of P.
The caps u.x+R l(z)>=0 pass through y. For one sufficiently large
finite R, boundedness of all finitely many K_z makes these caps empty
on every base outside F_p. On F_p their masses are exactly (1).
Their total is Gamma alpha. Undo the shear. QED.

## 2. A finite weighted-centerpoint lemma

Let h be any upper bound for the relative Helly number of P: every
finite family of ambient convex sets whose common intersection misses
P has a subfamily of at most h whose intersection misses P. For every
positive weight vector, there is a weighted base center at level M/h.

Here is the complete reduction. Consider all closed halfspaces A whose
retained weight is greater than (1-1/h)M. Any at most h of them have
a common point of P, since their omitted weights sum to less than M.
The Helly assumption implies every finite subfamily meets P. Because
P is finite, the whole family meets P: otherwise choose one excluding
member for each p. Let p be a point in the intersection. If a closed
halfspace H containing p had weight less than M/h, its open complement
would have weight greater than (1-1/h)M. Finiteness of P lets one
move its boundary slightly to a closed parallel halfspace inside that
open complement retaining all those points, contradicting the choice
of p. This proves the closed-halfspace assertion, including boundary
atoms. For h=1 the same argument is valid.

For a finite lattice-complete P=conv(P) intersect Z^n, one may take
h=2^n by classical Doignon, including the fixed set conv(P) in the
families if needed. The finite-set lemma above is the only weighted
extension being used; no mixed Grunbaum theorem is invoked.

## 3. Strictness from a base point outside all small faces

Assume h>1, put alpha=M/h, and let U be the union, within P, of all
proper faces F of B with w(F)<=alpha. If U differs from P, the actual
fiber family has a point of raw depth STRICTLY greater than
Gamma M/h. This includes every base with a point in relint(B), and
does not require that its chosen center have that base.

If U is empty, every weighted center from Section 2 has w(F_p)>alpha
(the full face has mass M>alpha); Section 1 proves the assertion.
Otherwise choose q in P outside U. For a sufficiently small epsilon>0
decrease each weight in U by epsilon and increase w_q by epsilon|U|,
leaving all other weights unchanged. The weights remain positive and
their total remains M.

Let delta be the minimum of alpha-w(A) over subsets A of P of weight
strictly less than alpha. This is a positive number: there are only
finitely many subsets, and the empty subset is eligible. Choose
2 epsilon|U|<delta as well as epsilon<min_{z in U}w_z. Any subset
with original weight below alpha still has new weight below alpha.
Thus every new alpha-center is an original alpha-center.

Each formerly small proper face excludes q and lies in U, so its new
weight is w(F)-epsilon|P intersect F|<alpha. No new alpha-center can
belong to that face, because an exposing halfspace would contradict
its depth. Section 2 supplies a new alpha-center p. Its original
minimal face consequently has weight greater than alpha. Section 1
gives strict depth at the actual point (p,g_p). QED.

For an actual mixed convex body with positive d-volume fibers, an
affine centroid graph, n>=1, and a positive-fiber integer base in the
relative interior of their hull, this proves strict OC. This is a
restricted regime, not a proof that a general bad minimum has such a
centroid graph or such an interior base.

## 4. Exact alternative when the perturbation cannot exclude all critical faces

Let F_1,...,F_m be the proper faces of weight exactly alpha=M/h.
If there is no signed vector v in R^P with

       sum_p v_p=0,  sum_{p in F_i}v_p<0 for every i,  (4)

then there are numbers theta_i>=0 satisfying

       sum_i theta_i 1_{P intersect F_i}(p)=1 for all p in P,
       sum_i theta_i=h.                               (5)

Conversely (5) prevents (4). This is a finite-dimensional alternative,
not an asserted geometric classification of the faces.

For a direct proof, let V={v:sum v_p=0} and let b_i be the orthogonal
projection of 1_{P intersect F_i} to V. A vector (4) exists exactly
when some v in V has v.b_i<0 for all i. If zero is outside the compact
convex hull of the b_i, take its nearest point b and v=-b. Minimality
gives b.b_i>=|b|^2>0, proving (4). If zero is in that hull, choose
lambda_i>=0, sum lambda_i=1, with sum lambda_i b_i=0. Then
sum lambda_i 1_{F_i}=c 1. Pairing with the original positive weights
gives alpha=cM, so c=1/h. Put theta_i=h lambda_i to get (5).
Conversely pair (5) with v in (4), obtaining 0<0. The empty-face-list
case has a vacuous (4), and no (5), as it should.

If (4) exists, a sufficiently small positive weight perturbation w+tv
preserves positivity and total mass, leaves every formerly subcritical
face below alpha, and makes all critical faces subcritical. The same
finite-subset-gap argument as Section 3 shows its weighted center is
an original center. Therefore Section 1 again gives strict depth.
Consequently equality in the affine-centroid mixed bound can occur
only if the proper critical faces admit the exact fractional partition
(5), unless h=1. This necessary condition is not sufficient: the
common ordinary-Grunbaum equality directions in Section 1 also matter.

## 5. Stability and scope

For a fixed finite base, the strict conclusion persists under small
Hausdorff changes of all positive fibers, even changes that destroy
the affine centroid graph. Fix the strict center's base p, choose
nearby points in its perturbed fiber, and note: the fiber indicators
converge in L1; the cap-mass error at a fixed point is uniformly bounded
by that total L1 error; moving a point by t within one fiber changes
nonvertical cap thresholds by at most t after normalizing the
continuous normal. Uniform boundedness bounds every such slab volume
by a fixed constant times t, summed over finitely many fibers. Vertical
caps are unaffected by that movement. Thus raw depth at these selected
actual points converges, while total mass converges. A strict gap
survives. This is a fixed-base local stability statement with a fully
tracked point, not an approximation argument resolving general OC.

The note treats full d-dimensional fibers. It makes no unproved claim
about globally nonparallel intrinsic affine spans. The boundary cases
n=0 and d=0 of OC are already handled separately in the main archive;
the present strictness statement deliberately assumes d>=1 and h>1.

## 6. One-sided extension to arbitrary centroid graphs

Independently PASS in
`unshared historical review/context (not an accepted premise)`.

There is a useful extension of the STRICTNESS implication which does
not assume an affine centroid graph. Let T={(z,g_z):z in P}, with its
same positive weights. If y=(p,g_p) is a weighted alpha-center of T
in its full ambient space, then its raw mixed depth is at least
Gamma alpha. If its minimal face F in conv(T) has weight greater than
alpha, its raw mixed depth is strictly greater than Gamma alpha.

Here are the changes needed in the proof, rather than an appeal to an
inadmissible nonaffine shear. A nonvertical cap through y is

       a.(z-p)+u.(x-g_p)>=0, |u|=1.

After writing x=g_z+xi separately inside each fiber, its threshold is

       t_{j,z}=-a_j.(z-p)-u_j.(g_z-g_p).

The retained centroid set is J={z:t_{j,z}<=0}; its weight is at least
alpha by the assumed ATOMIC full-ambient center property. Repeat the
finite sign pattern and extended-threshold limit argument of Section1.
Equality in the limiting lower bound forces w(J)=alpha, t_z=0 on J,
and thresholds bounded positively away from zero outside J. A positive
convex representation of y by ALL centroid points in its minimal face
gives sum lambda_z(z-p)=0 and sum lambda_z(g_z-g_p)=0. Therefore
sum lambda_z t_{j,z}=0 exactly, forcing that entire face into J.
Its weight is at least alpha by the same atomic center property and
an exposing ambient halfspace. Thus equality requires its weight to
be alpha, proving strictness when the weight is larger. No coordinate
map of the measured set was used. Vertical caps again have mass at
least alpha and cannot form an equality sequence since Gamma<1.

No converse is asserted in this extension: a general centroid-hull
face need not be exposed by a purely INTEGER-coordinate functional,
so isolating all its full fibers would require an additional argument.
This distinction is why the exact iff criterion in Section1 retains
the affine graph hypothesis.
